clue.text: Disorder makes bird land

indicators.note: disorder means jumbling, so the letters of makes and bird are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Some chaos causes a bird to come down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disorder' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the anagram signal working on MAKES BIRD.
explanation.definitionFit: To disembark is to leave a ship or aircraft and step onto shore, which is to land.

clue.text: Modern artist upset ancient Society

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word for ancient is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ancient means aged, very old

explanation.surface: A painter of the new school overturns an old learned body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Modern' may seem odd for a nineteenth-century painter, but Degas belongs to modern art as against the old masters.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Degas, the French Impressionist, counts as a modern painter against the old masters.

clue.text: Flats, etc, people go to view

definitions.meaning: flats are the painted canvas frames that make up a stage set
the landscape that tourists travel to look at

explanation.surface: Apartments and the like that visitors come to inspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flats' suggests apartments, but here it is the theatre sense: painted backdrops on a stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage backdrops and a pleasing landscape both carry this name, one theatrical and one natural.

clue.text: Army steps over a line about functioning of ruler

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the march sits above, ahead of, the following pieces
about means surrounding, so the first group of letters goes round the word for functioning

parts.note: soldiers' steps are a march
a machine that is functioning is on

explanation.surface: Troops march across a line while a ruler goes about his work.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' means the first piece sits above the rest; 'about' then wraps the whole run around the word for functioning.
explanation.definitionFit: Monarchal is the adjective for a monarch, a ruler, so it means belonging to a ruler.

clue.text: Came with Eric, on the move for so long from abroad

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: on the move means moving about, so the letters of Eric are shuffled

explanation.surface: Someone turned up with Eric, then headed off on a long journey overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the move' rearranges ERIC into ERCI.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrivederci is the Italian way of saying goodbye, a foreign version of the farewell so long.

clue.text: Book that's one among thousands

indicators.note: among means placed amid the other letters, here between the two thousands

parts.note: K and M are each abbreviations for a thousand, so two thousands give K and M
the Roman numeral I stands for one

explanation.surface: A single volume lost in a vast library.
explanation.walkthrough: K (from kilo) and M (Roman numeral) both mean a thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's novel about an orphan boy in India is titled with this name, so it is a book.

clue.text: Wood I cut initially? To be pedantic, it's chopped

parts.note: a log is a piece of wood

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the opening letter of cut is taken

explanation.surface: Someone splitting hairs over whether timber is cut or chopped.
explanation.walkthrough: To chop logic is an idiom for arguing in a pedantic, hair-splitting way; the definition is that idiom with this word as the thing chopped.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase 'chop logic' means to quibble pedantically, so reasoning is what gets chopped by a pedant.

clue.text: Comparatively feeble work by Debussy

definitions.meaning: more limp or weak, lame in the comparative
... is Debussy's orchestral piece about the sea

explanation.surface: A rather weak piece of music by the French composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Lame means weak, so the comparative is weaker; and Debussy wrote the symphonic sketches La Mer.

clue.text: It's uplifting for people when the balloon goes up

definitions.text: It's uplifting for people when the balloon goes up

parts.words: It's uplifting for people when the balloon goes up
parts.note: 'when the balloon goes up' usually means when trouble starts, but read literally it is the basket that carries passengers up under a hot-air balloon

explanation.surface: Something that cheers people up when the crisis breaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when the balloon goes up' is an idiom for when trouble begins; here it is literal, and 'uplifting' means carrying people aloft.
explanation.definitionFit: The car or basket slung beneath a balloon or airship that carries the passengers bears this name.

clue.text: Top position on board high-flier's at home in

parts.note: a crow is a bird, a high flier, and the possessive gives crow's
a bird at home is in its nest

explanation.surface: A high achiever is settled into a senior post on a company board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high-flier' suggests a high achiever and 'board' a company board, but it is a bird and a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A lookout platform at the top of a ship's mast is the highest station on board.

clue.text: Less experienced author given royalty

parts.note: Graham Greene was the English novelist
R, for rex or regina, stands for a king or queen

explanation.surface: A novelist receives payment on sales of his books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'royalty' looks like an author's payment, but it is R for a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means raw and untrained, so the comparative describes someone with less experience.

clue.text: Note from me to people inside

indicators.note: inside means the word for people is placed within the other letters

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
men means people

explanation.surface: A message passed from me to the folk indoors.
explanation.definitionFit: A memento is a reminder, a thing that serves as a note of something to remember.

clue.text: Insist son puts clothes on

parts.note: to wear clothes is to have them on

explanation.surface: A boy insists on dressing himself.
explanation.definitionFit: To swear something is to state it firmly, to insist it is true.

clue.text: Churchman promises to pay for what's second-hand

parts.note: a vicar is a parish priest, a churchman
an IOU is a note promising to pay a debt; IOUs is the plural

explanation.surface: A clergyman pledges money for a used item.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicarious experience is felt through another person, at second hand rather than directly.

clue.text: Colour pattern that's sweet on the band

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the word for sweet sits on top of the following piece

parts.note: candy is a sweet
a stripe is a band of colour

explanation.surface: A colourful design that is pleasing to the musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'band' suggests musicians, but it is a strip of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern of narrow coloured stripes on white, like a peppermint stick, is a design of colours.

clue.text: Letter that goes by air?

definitions.meaning: the name of the tenth letter of the alphabet, J
a bird, which travels through the air

explanation.surface: Correspondence sent by airmail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes by air' suggests airmail; it is a bird of the crow family.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the letter J is spelt this way, and the jay is a bird that flies.

clue.text: Patient types throw out petty official

parts.note: Job in the Bible is the byword for patience, so patient people are Jobs

indicators.note: out means disordered or wrong, so the letters of throw are rearranged

explanation.surface: People with endless patience cast out a minor bureaucrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'throw out' looks like a phrasal verb; 'out' alone is the anagram signal working on THROW, giving WORTH. A jobsworth is British slang for an official who sticks rigidly to petty rules.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for a minor functionary who obstructs people by insisting on the rules of his post.

clue.text: Retreat from scene of corporal punishment

definitions.meaning: a hideaway where one can go unseen
a place where someone gets a hiding, a beating

explanation.surface: Withdrawal from a place where beatings happen.
explanation.walkthrough: A hiding is British slang for a beating, so the second reading is where one is given.
explanation.definitionFit: A hideaway is a refuge or retreat, and read literally it is where a thrashing is given.

clue.text: Traveller's success introducing right garment for sportsmen

parts.note: Marco Polo was the famous Venetian traveller, so Polo's

indicators.note: introducing means bringing something in, so the letter for right goes inside the word for success

parts.note: a hit is a success

explanation.surface: A tourist's triumph is bringing in the right kit for athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'introducing' puts R inside HIT to give HIRT.
explanation.definitionFit: A collared short-sleeved knit top is named for the game of polo, so it is sportswear.

clue.text: Totally bare review producing heated argument

indicators.note: to review is to go over again, here re-viewing the letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A completely bare critique that sparks a fierce dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review' looks like a critic's write-up, but it is the anagram signal on TOTALLY BARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-for-all fight involving many combatants, used figuratively for a fierce quarrel.

clue.text: Furniture the average person won't overlook?

definitions.meaning: a lad of great height, whom someone of ordinary stature cannot see over

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture that an ordinary person will not fail to notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlook' means to fail to notice, but read literally it is seeing over the top of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A chest of drawers standing on a stand, and literally a lanky youth too high to see over.

clue.text: Save from boat going West

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means travelling right to left, so the word for boat is read backwards

parts.note: a tub is a slow, clumsy boat

explanation.surface: A rescue from a ship sailing westward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' means rescue in the surface, but it is the preposition meaning except.
explanation.definitionFit: Save as a preposition means except, as in 'all save one', a sense this word shares.

clue.text: Mexican food — it's consumed by an ass

indicators.note: consumed by means eaten up by, so the word for an ass swallows the other piece

parts.note: a burro is a small donkey, an ass
the it of it's gives the letters

explanation.surface: A Mexican dish that is eaten by a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla wrapped around a filling of meat or beans is a dish from Mexico.

clue.text: Water supply set up in good shape

parts.note: a well supplies water
something set up has been built

explanation.surface: A water supply has been installed in fine condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone with a sturdy, muscular physique is in good physical shape.

clue.text: Farm building I put in — a little one

indicators.note: put in means placed inside the word for farm building

parts.note: a barn is a farm building

explanation.surface: Into a barn I place a small child.
explanation.walkthrough: BAIRN is the Scots word for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish and northern English word for a child, a small youngster.

clue.text: Girl artist has turned around

indicators.note: around means the letters of has surround the artist
turned means reversed, so the whole combination is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
RA stands for Royal Academician, a painter

explanation.surface: A girl artist has spun round.
explanation.walkthrough: Two signals work in turn: 'around' wraps one piece about the other, and 'turned' then reads the result backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarah is a female first name, so it fits a girl.

clue.text: Vacation time for composer

parts.note: hols is British slang for holidays

explanation.surface: Holiday time for a musician.
explanation.definitionFit: Gustav Holst, writer of The Planets, was an English composer.

clue.text: Refuse to accept difficulty with mistake

parts.note: a rub is a difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'
bish is British slang for a mistake or blunder

explanation.surface: Someone declines to accept trouble along with an error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like the noun meaning waste, which the answer also means, but the definition is the verb phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To dismiss something as worthless, to reject it out of hand, is a slang verb sense.

clue.text: Show affection to unloved writer

indicators.note: love in tennis scoring is nil, the letter O, so unloved means that letter is removed

parts.note: Victor Hugo was the French novelist

explanation.surface: Being affectionate towards a writer nobody cares for.
explanation.definitionFit: To embrace someone is a physical way of showing fondness to them.

clue.text: For two of the three Rs, this is really different

definitions.text: For two of the three Rs, this is really different

parts.words: For two of the three Rs, this is really different
parts.note: the three Rs are reading, writing and arithmetic; for writing and arithmetic the opening letter is not really an R at all

explanation.surface: A remark that two of the basic school skills are very unlike the third.
explanation.walkthrough: The three Rs are reading, (w)riting and (a)rithmetic; only reading truly starts with R, so writing and arithmetic have a different opening letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening letter of a word is what differs: W and A instead of R.

clue.text: Composer's part in 15, roughly speaking

indicators.note: roughly speaking means said in a rough, approximate way, so a word said aloud gives the letters

parts.note: 15 across is a two-word answer meaning a retreat; its first part is hiding, said with the g dropped

explanation.surface: A piece of music, approximately put, plays a role in another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The first word of 15 across, said with a dropped g as 'hidin'', sounds like the composer's name. 'Composer's' means 'composer is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Haydn was the Austrian classical composer, father of the symphony.

clue.text: Expert in taking in firm's garment

indicators.note: taking in means enclosing, so the abbreviation for firm goes into the middle of the phrase

parts.note: to be expert in something is to be great at it
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A specialist in tailoring takes in a company's outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking in' sounds like a tailor's alteration to the garment, but it is the container signal splitting the phrase for 'Expert in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy overcoat, as worn by soldiers, is a piece of clothing.
